chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me from Ya'qub ibn Yazid from Hamad ibn Isa from Hariz and Fudhayl from Zurarah from Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Friday Prayer is obligatory, and gathering for it is obligatory with the Imam. So if a man leaves it for three Fridays without a valid reason, he has left three obligatory acts, and one who leaves three obligatory acts without a valid reason is a hypocrite. And he said: Whoever leaves the congregation out of preference for it and for the congregation of the believers without a valid reason, his prayer is not accepted.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on missing Friday Prayer for three consecutive weeks without a valid excuse?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights the gravity of congregational prayer by equating the omission of three Friday prayers without excuse to abandoning three fundamental obligations, a threshold often associated with the emergence of hypocrisy (munafiq). This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on communal unity under the Imam's leadership, where physical absence without valid reason signifies a spiritual disconnection from the body of believers.
